improvementsForChallenger: The ground is a flat mustard fill with faint stripes — no grass texture, flowers, clover, or ground cover anywhere; it reads as a graybox stage, not a meadow. Add painterly ground variation, patches, and scatter detail.

There is no coherent sun: trees, rocks, and fences cast no shadows onto the ground and receive almost no directional shading, so every environment prop floats. Add one consistent key-light direction with cast shadows and warm/cool separation.

Water is presented as hard-edged flat rectangles with visible plane borders (top-left stream, bottom-right dock) — these look like unfinished placement geometry; blend banks, add depth color and edge foam.

Cards sit on a thin offset drop shadow that reads as a UI decal rather than physical contact — add a tight contact shadow, visible edge thickness shading, and subtle ground-color bounce onto the card underside.
The teal sleeve borders on cast-verse cards clash with the parchment/olive/plum palette and fight the otherwise cohesive vintage look — retune them toward the field palette.
The tiny clipped card at the right edge of the opponent row is half cut off and unreadable at its rendered scale — fix the row layout so all cards fit and remain legible.

The environment is essentially a graybox: a flat mustard ground plane with visible horizontal banding stripes and zero ground cover between the tree ring and the play area. It needs an actual grass material, flowers/clutter, and painterly value variation before it reads as a meadow at all.

There is no coherent light: nothing on the field casts a shadow (trees, fence, rocks, cards all sit shadowless), so every object floats. Pick a sun direction and add unified cast shadows plus warm/cool grading.

Both water features (top-left and bottom-right corners) read as floating angular UI panels -- hard-edged blue polygons with loose cyan rectangles inside -- rather than ponds with banks that meet the ground. Resolve their shorelines and reflections.
The top-left fence rails hover with no contact shadow and the posts do not visibly meet the ground; ground every prop.
Cards are flat stickers: no edge thickness, near-invisible drop shadows, and deck stacks show no stacked-paper depth. Add card edges and contact-darkened shadows so cards sit on the world.

Palette and art cohesion: teal card sleeves and purple card backs fight the mustard field, and the card art is repeated silhouette screen-print (the same black cat on many cards). The typography and readable rules text are genuinely excellent -- keep that layer and bring the illustration/material quality up to match.
